chunk_findings.detail: The change replaces a read of the lease state field `expired_at` with `i.lease.live(time.time())`, and in doing so introduces a direct wall-clock read (`time.time()`, plus `import time` at line 11) into `recordquery.py`, which lives under `ddflow/services/doctypes/` and is not one of the lease modules. The regression test this change claims to close is `test_no_caller_outside_the_lease_modules_reads_the_clock_or_writes_a_release`: it asserts precisely that callers outside the lease modules do not read the clock. Whatever the checker's mechanism (AST scan for `time.time()`/`import time` against a lease-module whitelist, or the project's clock abstraction), the added `time.time()` call in a non-lease module is exactly the thing the test rejects, so on the very input that reproduces the bug (`_item_owner` invoked on any lease-bearing record) the test stays red / re-breaks. Additionally, if `live()` is the sanctioned encapsulation of lease liveness, the fix defeats it by supplying the clock from outside; the lease module should determine "now" itself (`i.lease.live()`), or the caller must use the project clock the lease modules are allowed to read, not `time.time()`.
